findings.title: YAML Unsafe Deserialization via yaml.CLoader Leading to Arbitrary Code Execution

data_flow.source: config.py:72 — open(config_file_path) reads YAML file content
data_flow.sink: config.py:80 — yaml.load(data, Loader=yaml.CLoader) deserializes with unsafe CLoader
data_flow.filter: NONE — CLoader is the C-based equivalent of yaml.Loader, which supports arbitrary Python object construction via !!python/object tags
data_flow.path: config_file_path → open() → data → yaml.load(CLoader) → arbitrary Python objects

findings.description: The config module uses yaml.CLoader to parse YAML configuration files. yaml.CLoader is the C implementation of yaml.Loader, NOT yaml.SafeLoader. It supports the full YAML tag set including !!python/object which allows instantiation of arbitrary Python classes. Any attacker who can modify the YAML config file can achieve remote code execution by crafting a YAML payload with malicious Python object tags.
findings.poc:
# Malicious config.yaml demonstrating RCE via !!python/object
# If placed at the CONFIG_PATH location (default: config.yaml):
PAYLOAD: !!python/object/apply:subprocess.check_output [['whoami']]

breakdown.AV: Local — attacker needs filesystem write access to config file
breakdown.AC: Low — crafting malicious YAML is trivial
breakdown.PR: None — no privileges needed beyond file write
breakdown.UI: Required — admin/user must load the malicious config

findings.title: Sensitive SQL Query Information Leakage via Hardcoded echo=True in Production

data_flow.sink: SQLAlchemy engine logs all SQL queries (including INSERT/UPDATE with sensitive data) to stdout via logging.StreamHandler
data_flow.filter: NONE — echo=True is a hardcoded boolean literal, cannot be disabled via configuration

findings.description: The DB class hardcodes echo=True when creating the async SQLAlchemy engine. This causes ALL SQL queries — including INSERT statements containing passwords, personal data, and other sensitive information — to be logged at INFO level to stdout via SQLAlchemy's logging system. There is no way to disable this behavior without modifying the framework source code. In production deployments, this exposes sensitive data to anyone with log access.
findings.poc:
# Any INSERT operation through the framework:
# await db.add(User(username='admin', password_hash='$2b$12$...'))
# This produces log output:
# 2025-01-01 00:00:00,000 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.Engine INSERT INTO users (username, password_hash) VALUES ('admin', '$2b$12$...')

fix.new:
echo = getenv("DB_ECHO", "false").lower() == "true"
        self._engine = create_async_engine(url, echo=echo, pool_pre_ping=True, pool_recycle=300, **options)

breakdown.AV: Local — logs are typically local files/stdout
breakdown.AC: Low — no special conditions needed, logging is automatic
breakdown.PR: Low — any user who can trigger DB operations
breakdown.C: Low — SQL queries leaked, may contain sensitive data
